title: Zak McKracken and the Alien Mindbenders
build: Commodore 64 original, three disks from the C64 Preservation Project's G64 collection: zak_mckracken_boot, _s1 and _s2 [activision_1988](manual)(!)

credits.by: David Fox, Matthew Kane, David Spangler and Ron Gilbert
Matthew Kane, Chris Grigg and David Warhol

tools.host: Linux 6.18 x86_64, cloud container with no display

include: the start-up copies a routine of the game's into the bottom of the stack page (from $823C)
the RAM under the I/O chips: the script interpreter's opcode table and code, copied there at start-up (from $9800 and $84D7)
exclude: copy source: the start-up copies these bytes to $CAD0, where they are described; nothing reads them here afterwards
copy sources: the start-up copies $77D9-$7858 to $F040 and $7859-$7C58 to $F800 (the character set), where they are described; the heap clear at $0442 then wipes them
the disk drive's own program: the start-up sends it to the 1541's RAM at $0500 with M-W commands and starts it with U3; coverage counts the computer's memory
copy sources: $823C-$82D6 goes to $0100, $82D7-$8AD6 to $D000 and $8A53-$909C to $F0C0, where they are described; the heap clear wipes them
filler at the end of the program file, alternating $00 and $FF as the RAM of the machine that saved it; nothing reads it
copy source: the start-up copies it to $82D7, from where it goes on to $D000 (the opcode table)
filler at the end of the program file, as at $909D
the top of the resource heap, which nothing has loaded into at start-up; rooms, scripts, costumes and sounds come in from the disk during play
